assumptions: Propagation: SGP4/SDP4 (satellite.js 7.x, Vallado 2006 reference implementation); both objects from mean elements (TLE epoch 2026-10-21T06:16:48.277Z, TLE epoch 2026-10-21T03:27:58.309Z).
Frame: TEME (True Equator Mean Equinox) Earth-centred inertial, km / km/s. Separation is the Euclidean norm of the TEME position difference; RIC components are relative to object A.
No manoeuvres, no atmospheric density updates beyond the B* term, no covariance. Typical TLE position errors are ~1 km at epoch, growing with age.
Minimum found by coarse sampling plus golden-section refinement; the result is a preliminary screening estimate, not a collision probability.
warnings: Objects move up to 442 km relative to each other between coarse samples; brief encounters could be under-sampled. Reduce the step for a finer screen.
frame: TEME (True Equator Mean Equinox) Earth-centred inertial, km / km/s
limitations: Preliminary screening estimate from public mean elements (TLE/OMM) propagated with SGP4; not a collision probability and not operational advice.
No covariance is available for TLEs, so probability-of-collision methods (Alfano, Foster, Chan) cannot be applied honestly here.
Miss distances of a few kilometres are within the uncertainty of TLE-based propagation; treat any flagged event as 'needs better data', not as a predicted collision.
